content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"Yes, the judge resolves a D6-vs-C1 collision by comparing the challenger's and defender's chains and their footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D6 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"'by footing, never verse by verse' can mean (1) no additional word-for-word naming test may defeat a footed chain, or (2) only contrary statements are retired, so positive naming may still be checked.","why":"The judge treats the challenger's footed chain as underdetermined because it does not explicitly name Joseph, adding a word-for-word positive-statement test instead of weighing chain against chain solely by footing."}
